To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
granulysin can be both a killer and a 'helper' molecule.
granulysin can be both a cytotoxic and immunomodulating molecule, and is involved in the response to tumours and infections.
granulysin functions in two distinct ways, firstly as a direct cytotoxic effector molecule, and secondly as an immune modulator.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the mechanisms of granulysins' dual role, the development of granulysine-based therapeutics and the identification of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of cancer, infection and autoimmunity.
understanding the mechanisms involved in the regulation of immune responses and the identification of molecules that can be used to enhance the immune system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
granulysin can be considered as a natural born killer, with an attractive side.
granulysin plays a dual role in the immune response to pathogens and tumours, both as a direct effector of cytotoxicity and as a potent immune 'alarmin'.
granulysin plays an important role in the immune system, both in the direct killing and elimination of pathogens, and in the modulation of the immune response to a pathogen or tumour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
granulysin may be an important molecule for both the innate and adaptive immune responses to infection or tumour and that further research is required to fully elucidate the role of this molecule.
granulysin can be considered as an 'attractive' molecule, in the sense that it attracts the immune system to a site of infection or tumour.

granulysin may not only be involved in killing infected or transformed cells, but also in orchestrating the response of the immune system to such infections or transformed cells, thus making granulysin an attractive molecule for future research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 15 Da isoform of granulysins has the potential to be developed as a vaccine adjuvant, or as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of cancer or chronic infection.
granulysin may not only play a role in the direct killing and elimination of tumour cells or infected cells, but also in the indirect stimulation of the immune response to these pathogens.
granulysin may have a role as a potential therapeutic agent, either alone or in combination with other drugs or vaccines.
